competitions.result: Third round — lost 3–2 away to Manchester City.
Second round — Vitória Setúbal advanced on away goals after a 3–3 aggregate draw. Liverpool lost 1–0 away and won 3–2 at Anfield.

overview: Liverpool finished fifth in the First Division with 51 points. Bobby Graham was their leading scorer with 21 goals in all competitions and played in all 54 competitive matches.

Roger Hunt left for Bolton Wanderers in December 1969, while Ray Clemence took over from Tommy Lawrence as first-choice goalkeeper in February. Clemence made 17 competitive appearances during the season; Ron Yeats, Ian St John and Peter Thompson remained regular members of the side.

The FA Cup run ended with a 1–0 quarter-final defeat away to Second Division Watford. In Europe, Liverpool beat Dundalk 10–0 at Anfield but went out of the Fairs Cup in the next round, losing to Vitória Setúbal on away goals after a 3–3 aggregate draw. Manchester City ended the League Cup campaign in the third round, leaving Liverpool without a trophy.

events.title: Ten goals against Dundalk
events.detail: Liverpool won 10–0 at Anfield in the first leg of their Fairs Cup first-round tie.

events.title: A 3–0 win at Goodison
events.detail: Liverpool beat Everton 3–0 away from home. Bobby Graham was among the scorers.

events.title: Watford end the FA Cup run
events.detail: A 1–0 defeat at Vicarage Road eliminated Liverpool in the quarter-final.

researchNotes: Graham’s 21 competitive goals and 54 appearances are corroborated by Liverpool FC’s obituary and LFChistory. Friendlies are excluded.
Whitham’s arrival came after Liverpool’s final league fixture and is included with 1970–71. Lindsay and Lloyd had signed during 1968–69 and are not duplicated here.
The Watford defeat is recorded without claiming that it alone caused the rebuilding of the team. Hunt had already departed, and changes in goal and personnel need their own chronology.
